title: Melanoma: reading the histology report, staging and margins

guidelineVersions: NICE NG14 Melanoma: assessment and management (published July 2015, last updated 27 July 2022)
RCPath G125 Dataset for histopathological reporting of primary cutaneous malignant melanoma (February 2019)
AJCC Cancer Staging Manual 8th edition melanoma staging (Gershenwald et al., 2017)

brief.scenario: Mr Graham Pellow, 58, had a changing 12 mm pigmented lesion excised from his left upper back two weeks ago. The histology report is back. He has no palpable lymph nodes. Written findings: before excision, the lesion was a 12 mm flat to slightly raised pigmented patch on the left upper back. Its two halves did not match in shape. The border was irregular and notched, with pigment fading out into the surrounding skin in places. The colour was mixed light brown, dark brown and black, with a small area of grey-blue.
brief.task: The examiner will read out the histology findings and then give you the report. Interpret them and answer questions on further management and on non-melanoma skin cancer.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Thickness and ulceration give the T stage; the stage drives margin, SLNB and BRAF.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Calling any melanoma over 1 mm stage II and taking a 2 cm margin.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "1.8 mm, not ulcerated: pT2a. With no clinical nodes that is stage IB."

grid.label: Breslow thickness
grid.fail: Cannot define it, or measures from the skin surface or the base of the epidermis.
grid.pass: From the top of the granular layer (or ulcer base) to the deepest invasive cell, in millimetres to 0.1 mm.
grid.high: Excludes microsatellites and periadnexal extension; notes mitotic index is still recorded as prognostic though no longer in the T category.

grid.label: Stages correctly
grid.fail: Calls a 1.8 mm non-ulcerated melanoma stage II.
grid.pass: 1.8 mm without ulceration is pT2a; with no clinical nodes this is stage IB.
grid.high: Ulceration would make it pT2b, stage IIA; a positive sentinel node would make it stage III.

grid.label: Excision margin
grid.fail: Takes a 2 cm margin because it is over 1 mm, or plans no further excision.
grid.pass: Wide local excision with a 1 cm clinical margin for stage I, measured around the biopsy scar.
grid.high: States 2 cm is for stage II, and 1 cm is used for stage II if 2 cm would cause unacceptable disfigurement or morbidity.

grid.label: Sentinel lymph node biopsy
grid.fail: Presents SLNB as curative, or orders imaging first.
grid.pass: Consider SLNB as Breslow is over 1.0 mm; a staging procedure, discussed with him. No imaging beforehand unless metastases suspected.
grid.high: If positive: stage III, CE-CT staging, and completion dissection not routinely offered.

grid.label: BRAF testing
grid.fail: Requests BRAF analysis on this stage IB primary as routine.
grid.pass: Not for stage IA or IB except in a trial; consider at IIA; carry out for IIB to IV.
grid.high: Would request BRAF analysis if the sentinel node is positive, because targeted therapy may then be relevant.

grid.label: Non-melanoma skin cancer
grid.fail: Treats basal cell carcinoma as having the same metastatic risk as melanoma.
grid.pass: BCC: basal keratinocytes, locally invasive, metastasis rare. SCC: keratinocytes, can spread to nodes. Melanoma: melanocytes, lymphatic and blood spread.
grid.high: Gives the clinical clues: pearly rolled edge and telangiectasia for BCC; keratotic, tender or ulcerated nodule for SCC.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The depth from the skin surface to the bottom of the lesion.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The report says 1.8 mm, no ulceration. What stage?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: A CT scan, then sentinel node biopsy to remove the cancer in the nodes.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: BRAF on the primary for everyone.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How does a basal cell carcinoma differ?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: It's another skin cancer; it spreads in the same way.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The distance from the top of the granular layer, or the ulcer base, to the deepest invasive cell, in millimetres to one decimal place.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The report says 1.8 mm, no ulceration, mitotic index 2 per mm². Stage it.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: pT2a. With no palpable nodes, stage IB.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Wide local excision with a 1 cm clinical margin around the scar, because it's stage I.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Would you do anything to the nodes?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'd consider sentinel lymph node biopsy because it's over 1.0 mm. It's a staging test, so I'd discuss it with him. No scan before it unless we suspect spread.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Should the primary have BRAF testing?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Not at stage IB unless he's in a trial. It's considered at IIA and done from IIB to IV.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How do BCC and SCC differ from melanoma?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: BCC is from basal keratinocytes: locally invasive, rarely metastasises. SCC can spread to nodes. Melanoma spreads by lymphatics and blood.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Microsatellites and extension down adnexa are excluded. Mitotic index isn't in the T category any more but is still recorded, because it predicts outcome.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Ulceration would make it pT2b, stage IIA, and a positive sentinel node would make it stage III.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: NICE reserves 2 cm for stage II. Even then, 1 cm is used if 2 cm would cause unacceptable disfigurement or morbidity.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: That's stage III. He'd have contrast CT staging, and NICE doesn't routinely offer completion lymph node dissection for a micrometastasis.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd now request BRAF analysis, because targeted therapy may become relevant.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How would you tell a BCC from an SCC clinically?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: BCC: pearly rolled edge with telangiectasia. SCC: a keratotic, often tender or ulcerated nodule.

failures.move: Staging a 1.8 mm non-ulcerated melanoma as stage II.
failures.consequence: Leads to an unnecessary 2 cm margin, BRAF testing and staging scans.

failures.move: Taking a 2 cm margin for stage IB disease.
failures.consequence: Larger defect, possibly needing a graft or flap, with no guideline support.
The patient consents to a staging test on false expectations.
Thickness, and therefore stage, is wrong.

recovery.line: I'd take the T stage from thickness and ulceration, then add node status: here pT2a, N0, stage IB.
The margin follows the stage, not the thickness alone.

knowledge.fact: Breslow: top of granular layer (or ulcer base) to deepest invasive cell, to 0.1 mm.
T2 is over 1.0 to 2.0 mm; 'a' means no ulceration. T2a N0 is stage IB; T2b N0 is IIA.
Margins: stage 0 at least 0.5 cm; stage I 1 cm; stage II 2 cm.
Consider SLNB over 1.0 mm, or 0.8 to 1.0 mm with ulceration, lymphovascular invasion or mitotic index of 2 or more.
BRAF on the primary: not IA or IB; consider IIA; do IIB to IV.

recall.think: Nodal and distant spread; wrong stage means wrong operation.
recall.say: "pT2a, stage IB: 1 cm wide local excision and discuss SLNB."
do: Offer SLNB discussion; no BRAF at IB

numbers.meaning: margin for stage I / stage II

recall.trap: Thickness over 1 mm does not by itself mean stage II.
recall.finish: Wide local excision, SLNB discussion, skin cancer MDT and follow-up.

partner.opening: You have the written findings of the lesion before excision. Which features worry you, and why? Then I'll read out the histology findings.

reveals.finding: Read out: the H&E section shows an intact epidermis with a distinct granular layer and no ulceration. Atypical melanocytes lie singly and in nests along the junction between epidermis and dermis, and single cells extend upward into the upper epidermis. Nests and sheets of atypical melanocytes invade the dermis, the deepest invasive cells lying well below the junction. Where would the pathologist measure the thickness from and to?
Superficial spreading melanoma, Breslow 1.8 mm, no ulceration, mitotic index 2/mm², no lymphovascular invasion, no microsatellites, peripheral and deep margins clear.
No palpable nodes in either axilla or the neck.
SLNB shows a micrometastasis in one axillary node.

push.question: What margin would you take, and why?
What is the role of sentinel node biopsy?
Would you send the primary for BRAF testing?
push.expect: No at IB, except in a trial.

curveballs.prompt: The lesion is on his face and 1 cm would distort the eyelid.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Discuss with the specialist skin cancer MDT; consider specialist reconstruction or alternative approaches rather than compromising care alone.

curveballs.prompt: What if the report had said ulceration present?
curveballs.safeAnswer: pT2b, stage IIA: 2 cm margin, consider SLNB, consider BRAF analysis.
Anatomical level of invasion; superseded by Breslow thickness, which is more reproducible.
